milestones.label: Late Miocene Cooling & C4 Savanna Expansion (~7–5.5 Ma)
milestones.summary: Global ocean cooling (~3–4 °C warmer than today) accompanies tropical C4 grassland expansion in East Africa and Sahel around the earliest hominins (Sahelanthropus, Orrorin, Ardipithecus).
milestones.humanContext: Mosaic woodland–savanna habitats emerge as earliest hominins diverge across Chad, Kenya, and Ethiopia.
milestones.caution: Regional aridification varied strongly by basin; continental proxy coverage before 5 Ma is sparser than Quaternary cores.

milestones.label: Intensification of Northern Hemisphere Glaciation (~2.7 Ma)
milestones.summary: LR04 benthic d18O rises sharply as 41-kyr obliquity cycles begin driving large Arctic & sub-Arctic ice sheets and global sea-level swings of ~40–60 m.
milestones.humanContext: Coincides with Oldowan stone tools (Lomekwi/Gona), early Homo emergence, and Australopithecus diversification.
milestones.caution: Climate shifts created alternating wet/dry pulses rather than a single linear drying trend.

milestones.label: Mid-Pleistocene Transition (~1.25–0.7 Ma)
milestones.summary: Earth's glacial rhythm shifts without a change in orbital forcing from 41-kyr cycles to deep ~100-kyr ice ages (~100–125 m sea-level drops).
milestones.humanContext: Follows early Eurasian dispersals (Dmanisi, Java, Nihewan, Europe) and precedes classic Middle Pleistocene Acheulean sites.
milestones.caution: Transition unfolded over ~500 kyr rather than a sudden single event.

milestones.label: MIS 12 Extreme Glacial (~450 ka)
milestones.summary: One of the cold extreme glacials of the past million years (~−125 m sea level); proglacial lake drainage breaches the Strait of Dover chalk ridge.
milestones.humanContext: Contemporary with Sima de los Huesos and early Eurasian pre-Neanderthals.
milestones.caution: Benthic d18O mixes global ice volume and deep-water temperature.

milestones.label: Last Interglacial Peak (Eemian / MIS 5e, ~129–116 ka)
milestones.summary: Global temperatures reach ~+0.5 to +1.5 °C above pre-industrial, Greenland and West Antarctic ice shrink, and sea level peaks ~+6 to +9 m.
milestones.humanContext: Broad woodland belt spans Europe (Neanderthals at Krapina/Neumark-Nord) while Humid Arabian/Saharan corridors open for early Homo sapiens (Skhul/Qafzeh).
milestones.caution: Peak warmth was geographically uneven and lagged orbital insolation.

milestones.label: MIS 4 Glacial Expansion (~72–58 ka)
milestones.summary: Sea level drops ~−85 m, dramatically narrowing Wallacean water crossings and merging Java–Sumatra–Borneo (Sundaland) and Australia–New Guinea (Sahul).
milestones.humanContext: Major Out-of-Africa dispersal window and earliest dated Australian rock-shelter occupations (~65–50 ka).
milestones.caution: Sea-level curves carry ±10–15 m global error bars and local isostatic variations.

milestones.label: Rapid Dansgaard–Oeschger & Heinrich Swings (~60–25 ka)
milestones.summary: Greenland ice cores show abrupt 5–8 °C North Atlantic warming jumps within decades followed by century-to-millennial cooling during MIS 3.
milestones.humanContext: Coincides with Upper Paleolithic dispersals into Eurasia and the final documented Neanderthal horizons (~45–39 ka).
milestones.caution: Abrupt Greenland spikes were strongly amplified in the North Atlantic compared with tropical hemispheres.

milestones.label: Last Glacial Maximum (~23–19 ka)
milestones.summary: Global mean temperature ~−6 °C below pre-industrial, CO2 ~185–190 ppm, and global sea level ~−125 m below today, uniting Siberia with Alaska (Beringia).
milestones.humanContext: Populations contract toward southern Eurasian refugia while Beringian / Pacific rim corridors frame early peopling of the Americas.
milestones.caution: Ice-free corridors and coastal kelp routes opened asynchronously between ~17–14 ka.

milestones.label: Bølling Warming & Meltwater Pulse 1A (~14.7–14.2 ka)
milestones.summary: Rapid deglacial warming drives ~15–20 m of global sea-level rise within ~400–500 years as ice sheets collapse.
milestones.humanContext: Marks accelerating coastal submergence of Sundaland, Beringia, and North Sea lowlands alongside Late Pleistocene Americas settlements.
milestones.caution: Individual coral reef terraces constrain MWP-1A amplitude but vary by far-field GIA response.

milestones.label: Younger Dryas Stadial (~12.9–11.7 ka)
milestones.summary: Abrupt return to near-glacial cold in North Atlantic & Europe as AMOC weakens, terminating sharply ~11.7 ka at the start of the Holocene.
milestones.humanContext: Precedes Natufian–Early Neolithic sedentary transitions and correlates with cooling/drying stresses across northern latitudes.
milestones.caution: Antarctic cores warm while Greenland cools (bipolar seesaw); not uniformly cold worldwide.

milestones.label: African Humid Period & 8.2 ka Cooling Event (~10–5.5 ka)
milestones.summary: Stronger summer orbital insolation sustains vegetated Sahara lakes & savanna corridors, punctuated by a ~150-yr 8.2 ka cold anomaly from Lake Agassiz drainage.
milestones.humanContext: Saharan pastoralism (Takarkori/Gobero) and early Eurasian/Yangtze agriculture expand; Doggerland submerges beneath the North Sea.
milestones.caution: Global Holocene temperature reconstructions differ slightly between proxy compilations and climate models.

milestones.label: Mid-to-Late Holocene Transition / 4.2 ka Aridification (~2250 BCE)
milestones.summary: Sahara–Arabian–Indus monsoon weakening marks the end of humid Saharan conditions and widespread regional hydroclimate shifts.
milestones.humanContext: Overlaps Old Kingdom Egypt, Akkadian Mesopotamia, and mature Indus urbanization transformations without implying single-factor collapse.
milestones.caution: Signal strength is regional (strongest in monsoon/Mediterranean zones), modest in global mean temperature.

milestones.label: Late Antique Little Ice Age (536–541 CE Volcanic Cluster)
milestones.summary: Twin–triple volcanic sulfate spikes recorded in Greenland & Antarctic ice cores plus severe European/Asian tree-ring growth narrowing.
milestones.humanContext: Documented by Mediterranean and East Asian chroniclers as an 18-month solar dimming followed by cold summers.
milestones.caution: Direct human casualties depended heavily on local harvests, grain stores, and trade networks.

milestones.label: Medieval Climate Anomaly (~950–1250 CE)
milestones.summary: PAGES 2k multiproxy synthesis shows warm episodes that peaked regionally at different centuries rather than a globally synchronous warm plateau.
milestones.humanContext: Coincides with Norse North Atlantic expansion and warm Pacific voyages before Pacific/American drought transitions.
milestones.caution: Peak warmth was neither globally uniform nor warmer than 20th-century industrial decades.

milestones.label: Little Ice Age Coldest Phase (~1570–1710 CE)
milestones.summary: Clustered tropical volcanism (Samalas 1257, Kuwae 1452, Huaynaputina 1600) and solar minima cool global mean temperature ~−0.3 to −0.5 °C below mid-Holocene baselines.
milestones.humanContext: Alpine glaciers advance across Europe; tree rings and Gergis & Fowler (2009) ENSO tables document severe drought/frost oscillations.
milestones.caution: Cooling magnitude was ~1–1.5 °C regionally in Europe/North America but ~0.3–0.5 °C in the global mean.

milestones.label: 1815 Tambora Eruption & 1816 'Year Without a Summer'
milestones.summary: VEI 7 eruption in Indonesia injects massive stratospheric aerosols, dropping 1816 PAGES 2k global temperature sharply alongside Europe/New England crop failures.
milestones.humanContext: Links directly to the Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program entry in the atlas natural-hazard catalog.
milestones.caution: Post-1850 warming accelerates toward the 1900 CE end of the atlas historical scope.

landbridges.name: Torres Strait & Bass Strait (Sahul)
landbridges.summary: Australia, New Guinea, and Tasmania unite into Greater Sahul whenever sea level falls below ~−12 to −55 m; flooded by ~8–9 ka.

landbridges.name: Strait of Dover (Britain–Continent)
landbridges.summary: Britain connects overland to continental Europe until rising meltwater breaches the Channel ~8.5–8.0 ka.

landbridges.name: Doggerland (Southern North Sea)
landbridges.summary: Broad Mesolithic lowland linking England, Denmark, and Netherlands; mostly inundated by ~8.2–7.5 ka.

landbridges.name: Bering Land Bridge (Siberia–Alaska)
landbridges.summary: Broad plain connecting Northeast Asia and Alaska during glacials (~70–58 ka & ~30–11 ka) below −50 m sea level.

landbridges.name: Sundaland (Malay–Sumatra–Java–Borneo)
landbridges.summary: Exposes an extra >1.8 million km² of Southeast Asian shelf below −60 m, leaving narrow Wallacean sea crossings even at LGM.
